content.text: As you build your website, you will encounter some technical terms. Refer to this list whenever you see a word you do not recognize.

rows: Web Browser
The software application you open to view pages on the internet. Examples include Chrome, Safari, and Edge.
Search Engine
A specialized website (like Google or Bing) that helps you find other websites by typing in keywords.
URL (Web Address)
The unique text you type to go directly to a website (e.g., www.google.com).
Address Bar
The long, white text box at the very top of your browser window where the URL is displayed.
Server
A powerful computer, located far away, that stays turned on 24 hours a day to store website files and send them to visitors.
Web Hosting
The service of storing your website's files on a server so the public can access them.
GitHub
A website that provides free hosting for web files and code.
Repository (or Repo)
A dedicated folder inside your GitHub account that holds all the files for one specific website project.
Fork
The process of making an exact copy of someone else's GitHub repository (folder) and placing it into your own GitHub account so you can edit it.
Workspace
A digital desktop or area where you can safely edit and test your website's files without changing the live, public version of your website until you are ready.
Version

A saved state of your website files at a specific point in time. Much like having 'Draft 1' and 'Draft 2' of a document, it allows you to keep track of changes and go back to an older setup if you make a mistake.
Branch
A version or 'workspace' within a repository. A repository can have multiple branches, each containing different versions of the website's files.
JSON

Short for JavaScript Object Notation. It is a simple text format used to store information. It looks like a list of labels and answers (for example: "name": "Jane"), making it easy to edit your website's content without writing complex code.
Commit
The process of saving your changes to your files on GitHub.
Domain name
The unique, user-friendly address people type into a browser to find your website on the internet. Such as (google.com)
